title: Graph Diffusion
text: Network diffusion propagates node-level signals (e.g. gene-level scores) across graph using kernel derived graph Laplacian. intuition straightforward: node carries strong signal, neighbours inherit signal, strength decaying graph distance increases. useful tasks based “guilty association” principle, handful known disease genes want find additional candidates well-connected protein-protein interaction network. genewalkR implements five spectral kernels diffusion literature: Regularised Laplacian: $(\\sigma^2 L + \\alpha )^{-1}$ Commute time: Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse LL Diffusion (heat): $\\exp(-\\sigma^2 / 2 \\cdot L)$ Inverse cosine: $\\cos(\\pi/4 \\cdot \\lambda)$ p-step: (aI−L)p(aI - L)^p three scoring methods: Raw: direct kernel-weighted scores Z-score: analytically normalised scores permutation null Monte Carlo (heatrank): empirical p-values via permutation testing entire computation performed Rust via spectral decomposition Laplacian, dense kernel matrix never materialised. work based diffuStats package. start square lattice build intuition. lattice, graph distance easy reason , can verify diffusion scores decay expected. Run kernel: place unit signal corner node diffuse across network. lattice, expect scores decay monotonically shortest-path distance source.  Since square lattice, can visualise scores heatmap.  can see nicely grid network bottom left area graph getting diffusion heat original source node. can compare three scoring approaches input:  Real biological networks (PPI, gene regulatory) tend scale-free: nodes connections, small number hubs highly connected. can simulate Barabasi-Albert preferential attachment model. generate random network first…  can appreciate nodes connections, majority edges network. pick handful “seed genes” (mimicking known disease associations gene function) diffuse signal across network prioritise candidate genes. can clearly appreciate seed genes heat, followed neighbours. can also investigate top candidates seed genes explore relationship node degree resulting Z-scores:  Different kernels emphasise different aspects network topology. diffusion kernel large bandwidth spreads signal broadly, whilst regularised Laplacian conservative. synthetic example however, tiny difference s  DiffusionScores workflow separates kernel construction scoring, can build kernel run multiple diffusions different inputs methods without recomputing spectral decomposition. large networks (> 2000 nodes), truncated strategy avoids dense eigenvalue decomposition entirely, using iterative Lanczos solver scales networks tens thousands nodes.

top 3 hubs   sample(names(deg[deg <= 3]), 2) # 2 peripheral nodes ) cat("Seed genes:", paste(seed_genes, collapse = ", "), "

input: seed genes get score 1, rest is background all_genes <- V(g_sf)$name input_sf <- stats::setNames(   ifelse(all_genes %in% seed_genes, 1.0, 0.0),   all_genes )  obj_sf <- diffuse_scores(obj_sf, input = input_sf, method = "z") results <- get_scores(obj_sf) setorder(results, -input_1)  head(results, 20) #>         node    input_1 #>       <char>      <num> #>  1:   gene_5 10.3986239 #>  2: gene_472 10.1696624 #>  3: gene_249 10.1351093 #>  4:   gene_4  9.9473892 #>  5:   gene_1  9.8849507 #>  6: gene_236  1.5813897 #>  7: gene_211  1.0957907 #>  8: gene_230  0.9027809 #>  9:  gene_69  0.8638611 #> 10:  gene_28  0.5907598 #> 11: gene_279  0.5877281 #> 12: gene_197  0.5488474 #> 13: gene_183  0.4741730 #> 14: gene_368  0.4495234 #> 15: gene_345  0.4313139 #> 16:  gene_29  0.4235714 #> 17: gene_168  0.4218336 #> 18: gene_305  0.4056889 #> 19: gene_358  0.3872085 #> 20: gene_290  0.3863111 #>         node    input_1 #>       <char>      <num> results[, is_seed := node %in% seed_genes] results[, rank := .I] results[, degree := deg[node]]  # text: Generates synthetic network mimics real GeneWalk input data testing benchmarking. network consists three components: hierarchical ontology (tree structure lateral edges), gene--ontology annotations, protein-protein interactions (PPI).
